subject: Results differed from mplus using covariance matrix as input

messages.author: 46884d82c482ddd8
messages.subject: Results differed from mplus using covariance matrix as input
parts:
Hi,

I was trying to replicate Mplus example in Lavaan. As I tried to use a covariance matrix as input, I got different likelihood ratio test results (LL = -1348.059) from Mplus (-634.972). 

Below is my r code:
# read covariance matrix
lower <- '
18.300,
38.972,   196.116,
27.392,   80.172,   294.866,
25240.080, 68797.683, 91628.810, 94206882.35,
-0.448,   -1.111,   -1.280,   -975.008,   0.250'

regression.cov <- getCov(lower,names=c("time","pubs","cits","salary","female"))

model.1 <- 'salary ~ time + pubs + cits + female'

fit.cov <- sem(model.1, sample.cov=regression.cov, sample.nobs=62, meanstructure=TRUE)
summary(fit.cov, standardize = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)


I have the same issue with using a correlation matrix as input, I use the code:
corr <- '
1,
0.651, 1,
0.373, 0.333, 1,
0.608, 0.506, 0.550, 1,
-0.210, -0.159, -0.149, -0.201, 1'
sd <- c(4.278,14.004,17.172,9706.023,0.500)
sample.cor <- getCov(corr)
corrsd <- cor2cov(sample.cor,sd,names = c("time","pubs","cits","salary","female"))

Lavaan gives me the same likelihood results for the two analysis. But they all differ from Mplus. I have attached the Mplus output syntax for reference. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Results differed from mplus using covariance matrix as input
parts:
There are huge differences in the variances of your measures. It's typically suggested that you keep the variances within an order of magnitude. This might be causing problems for Mplus, or lavaan, or both.

Jeremy

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Results differed from mplus using covariance matrix as input
parts:
On 8/26/19 5:38 PM, Ye Feng wrote:
> I was trying to replicate Mplus example in Lavaan. As I tried to use a
> covariance matrix as input, I got different likelihood ratio test
> results (LL = -1348.059) from Mplus (-634.972).

I believe this is a (small) bug in lavaan. It gives you the
loglikelihood of the 'joint' distribution (all variables), while Mplus
gives you the loglikelihood of 'y' only, treating 'x' as fixed.

In fact, lavaan uses the same logic ... except if the input is a
covariance matrix, instead of full data. I will correct this in a future
update.

Yves.
